messages:
ana: Quick follow-up to the streaming + retry RFC — I sketched a simplified ingress retry state machine that (hopefully) reduces cross-service handshake complexity. want feedback on safety and rollout.
chris: SG. TL;DR of change?
sasha: yes please, short bullets.
ana: Goals: 1) move from multi-hop resume tokens between frontdoor<->proxy<->upstream to a single-source-of-truth owned by the gateway; 2) treat streaming retries as a short-lived reconnection with preserved idempotency keys and optional suffix-resume token; 3) remove midstream lease transfers as an optimization not required for correctness.
jun: sounds like big win for complexity. risk: increased gateway memory for holding resume windows, right?
ana: right — we keep only a compact checkpoint per active request: last emitted token index + small KV of sent prefixes. bounded by request-configured resume_window (default 2s / 4k tokens). eviction policy: LRU or on-conn-close.
mike: how does client behave? do we require clients to re-send idempotency-key + offset when reconnecting?
ana: yes. client contract: on reconnect supply same idempotency-key and optional resume_offset. gateway validates offset <= checkpoint and resumes if within window, otherwise fall back to full replay (idempotent semantics) or reject.
sasha: what about non-idempotent side effects? we need a hard guarantee: if upstream may have committed side effects, resuming could duplicate. we should gate resume with a header like `X-Resume-Safe: true` from client and require server opt-in.
ana: agreed. default: `X-Resume-Safe: false` so no implicit resume for side-effectful requests. add a route-level config to opt into resume semantics.
jun: instrumentation and metrics we need: resume_attempts_total, resume_success_total, resume_fallsback_total, resume_latency_ms. also per-route accept_rate and memory_pressure.
ana: added to plan. also need to export `resume.window_bytes` gauge for SLO watching.
chris: rollout plan idea: implement gateway-owned checkpointing but keep resume disabled by default. then enable for internal services only (flag `feature.resume.gateway`) in staging, run 1% canary in prod, 10%, 50%, GA. this avoids cross-service coordination.
mike: what about backward compatibility for older proxies that expect the resume token handshake? we have many edge sidecars in Dedicated clusters.
ana: compatibility mode: gateway will accept legacy resume tokens but will translate into internal checkpoint structure. we'll keep a translator module for one release cycle.
sasha: we should also simplify the handshake protocol. proposal:

```
Client -> Gateway: POST /generate (Idempotency-Key, X-Resume-Safe, Resume-Offset?)
Gateway -> Upstream: normal streaming request (no resume token header)
On transient failure: Client reconnects with same Idempotency-Key + Resume-Offset
Gateway: if checkpoint exists and offset <= checkpoint, proxy resumes by piping KV cache + offset to upstream via existing streaming API; else return 409/resume-required
```

That avoids multi-hop tokens and keeps the gateway authoritative.
jun: small nit: how do we convey partial tokens to upstream? we currently rely on a `Resume-Token` opaque blob that upstream uses to reconstruct KV cache. if we remove that, upstreams must accept `prefix_len` + `prefix_hash` and reconstruct. is that doable for large models?
ana: for large kvcache, we don't ship raw cache. instead we ship an immutable checkpoint reference stored in shared object store (S3) with short TTL; gateway writes checkpoint on first suspend and references it via `X-Checkpoint-Ref` to upstream. upstreams fetch if they need to resume.
mike: storing checkpoints off-host introduces latency and cost. tradeoffs: additional S3 ops vs simpler handshake. suggest local in-memory cache with fallback to object store when memory pressure high.
ana: agreed. default: in-memory local checkpoint, fallback to s3 when memory limit hit. add config: `checkpoint.storage_policy`.
sasha: how about security / PII? checkpoint blobs must be encrypted and have ACLs. add KMS integration and per-tenant namespaces.
ana: noted.
chris: testing matrix: unit tests for state machine, integration tests simulating midstream aborts, chaos tests with network partitions, and canary e2e with internal traffic.
ana: QA: can we add `qa-bot` to automatically run the integration suite when branch pushed? infra-bot already posts deploys.
infra-bot: Deploy hook triggered: branch `gateway/resume-simplify` built and deployed to staging (ami: infra-1792). run_id: ci-78234.
mike: awesome — once staging passes let's flip `feature.resume.gateway` for internal routes. also coordinate with Dedicated ops to ensure sidecars get translator module in the same release window.
jun: docs: update API page for streaming with the new reconnection contract, add example client code for reconnect that sets `Resume-Offset` and retries gracefully.
sasha: one more tradeoff: hedging. if we do early hedging to multiple upstreams, resume semantics conflict. recommend: disallow hedging for routes with resume enabled (route config). or make hedging use independent idempotency semantics.
ana: agree: default `hedging: disabled` when `resume: enabled` to avoid duplicate token ambiguity.
chris: next steps: ana to open PR with code + tests, include a design doc summarizing the state machine and compatibility plan. assign reviewers: @chris, @sasha, @mike, @jun.
ana: will do. thanks everyone :heart: Any strong objections to this direction? if none by EOD I’ll start the PR.
sasha: no objections from me.
mike: :+1:
jun: +1
chris: go for it.
qa-bot: Integration suite queued: build ci-78234 -> tests: streaming-reconnect (12), kvcache-checkpoint (8). results will post here.
qa-bot: streaming-reconnect: 12 passed, kvcache-checkpoint: 8 passed.
ana: sweet — starting PR now. will tag reviewers and the rollout checklist in the PR description.
